name: Beard transplant

card.summary: Follicular unit grafts moved to the jaw and cheeks to fill patchy or absent facial hair; described in surgical reviews as a refined procedure, with outcome data limited to surgeon-reported series.
card.aka: facial hair transplant, beard hair restoration
card.note: Published evidence is surgeon-authored reviews and experience reports; no controlled trials were found.

quick.overview:
A beard transplant moves hair follicles, usually from the scalp, into areas of the face where beard growth is sparse or absent. It is a branch of hair restoration surgery and uses the same graft-based techniques as scalp transplantation, with small recipient sites angled to match natural beard direction.

Surgical reviews describe it as having grown in importance because of its natural-looking results. The available literature consists mainly of surgeon experience, such as one review reporting more than 700 primary beard transplants by a single author, rather than controlled studies.
quick.mechanism: Grafts containing one or two hairs are harvested, trimmed to a minimal cuff of skin and placed into tiny recipient sites using the smallest possible blades, with angulation and design chosen to look natural. Transplanted hair is expected to keep the traits of its donor area.
quick.risks: Reviews discuss reparative procedures for poor results, and general hair-transplant risks such as swelling, scarring and infection apply. A looksmaxxing-specific evidence base is absent; no forum material is cited here.

lead: Beard transplantation is the surgical relocation of hair follicles, usually taken from the scalp, to areas of the face where facial hair is thin, patchy or absent. It sits within hair restoration surgery alongside eyebrow, sideburn and eyelash transplantation [1][2].

A 2024 review by a surgeon with experience of more than 700 primary beard transplants and many repair procedures states that restoring the beard area has become an important part of hair restoration surgery because of its natural-appearing results, and emphasizes careful graft dissection, acute angulation of recipient sites and aesthetic design [1]. A 2013 review similarly describes beards, goatees and sideburns as popular procedures whose results can be outstanding [2].
The evidence consists of expert reviews and personal series. No controlled trials of beard transplantation were found.
infobox: Scalp (FUE or FUT); body hair is sometimes used [3]
About US$3,000-7,000 for partial and $15,000 or more for full beards, per Grokipedia [3]

paras: According to a 2024 review, key aesthetic steps include dissecting grafts so that one- and two-hair grafts have a minimal cuff of surrounding skin, making recipient sites with the smallest possible blades at acute angles and appropriate direction, and planning the beard's design [1]. The review also covers beard-to-scalp hair restoration, in which beard hair is used as a donor source for the scalp [1].

Grokipedia, an AI-generated source treated with caution, says follicles are typically taken from the scalp by FUE or FUT, that body hair can be a less reliable donor, and that results begin around three to four months with fuller results at about a year [3].

The reviews describe natural-looking results as achievable by an experienced surgeon [1][2]. They discuss repair of poorly executed work, indicating that results depend on technique [1]. Grokipedia lists swelling, scarring and infection among risks, as with scalp transplantation [3]. No published trial compares outcomes across techniques or clinics.
No studies found of beard transplantation beyond surgeon-reported reviews [1][2]. A registered trial of follicular unit extraction for alopecic scars (not specific to the beard) exists [4].
